name: ai-summary-gotcha-inline-vs-standalone
hook: Inline Gotcha: in @ai-summary matches sibling payment files
body: For AI-summary doc blocks in this codebase, inline `Gotcha:` prose inside `@ai-summary` is preferred over a standalone `@gotcha` JSDoc tag when sibling files use the inline form. This maintains visual consistency across a module.
why: stripe.ts and paypal.ts both use inline Gotcha: prose in their @ai-summary blocks. env.ts used a standalone @gotcha tag — a style gap flagged in PR #136 review. Aligning env.ts by folding the gotcha into @ai-summary resolves the inconsistency with minimal diff.
how_to_apply: When adding gotcha notes to @ai-summary blocks, prefer inline `Gotcha:` prose. Reserve standalone `@gotcha` tags for cases where no @ai-summary exists or where the gotcha applies to the whole file rather than a specific function.

name: gotcha-must-match-actual-api-behavior
hook: Gotcha claims about API behaviour must be verified against the actual API
body: The cancelStripeCheckout gotcha in stripe.ts claimed Stripe's expire API is a 'no-op' on already-expired sessions — but Stripe actually throws `resource_already_expired`. The error was safely caught at route.ts:204 so there was no runtime crash, but the documentation was wrong. A reviewer caught it. Gotcha claims about third-party API behaviour need to be verified against actual API semantics, not assumed.
why: A wrong gotcha misleads developers about actual API semantics. In this case the runtime was safe because the error was caught, but a wrong gotcha elsewhere could cause someone to not handle a real error correctly.
how_to_apply: When writing a gotcha about third-party API behaviour, verify against the actual API docs or behaviour. If uncertain, describe what the code does (catches and handles) rather than what the API guarantees.
